results.snippet: partitioning large power-law graphs under memory constraints ruben mayer technical university of munich ruben.mayer@tum.de abstract distributed systems that manage and process graph-structured data internally solve a graph partitioning problem to minimize their com- munication overhead and query run-time. besides computational complexity—optimal graph partitioning is np-hard—another im- portant consideration is the memory overhead. real-world graphs often have an immense size, such that loading the complete graph into memory for partitioning is not economical or feasible. cur- rently, the common approach to reduce memory overhead is to rely on streaming partitioning algorithms. while the latest streaming algorithms lead to reasonable partitioning quality on some graphs, they are still not completely competitive to in-memory partitioners. in this paper, we propose a new system, hybrid edge partitioner (hep), that can partition graphs that fit partly into memory while yielding a high partitioning quality. hep can flexibly adapt its memory overhead by separating the edge set of the graph into two sub-sets. one sub-set is partitioned by ne++, a novel, efficient in-memory algorithm, while the other sub-set is partitioned by a streaming approach. our evaluations on large real-world graphs show that in many cases, hep outperforms both in-memory parti- tioning and streaming partitioning at the same time. hence, hep is an attractive alternative to existing solutions that cannot fine- tune their memory overheads. finally, we show that using hep, we achieve a significant speedup of distributed graph processing jobs on spark/graphx compared to state-of-the-art partitioning algorithms. ccs concepts • information systems → graph-based database models; • the- ory of computation → graph algorithms analysis. keywords graph partitioning; distributed graph processing acm reference format: ruben mayer and hans-arno jacobsen. 2021. hybrid edge partitioner: parti-
results.title: Hybrid Edge Partitioner: Partitioning Large Power-Law Graphs under Memory Constraints

results.snippet: A Note on Edge-based Graph Partitioning and its Linear Algebraic StructureLinear algebraEdge-centric representationGraph partitioningComputational complexityWe analyze two essential problems arising from edge-based graph partitioning. We show that one of them is an NP-hard problem but the other is in P, presenting a novel methodology that links linear algebra theory to the graph problems as a part of proving the facts. This is a significant trial in that linear algebra, which has been mostly adopted as a theoretical analysis tool, is practically applied to solving actual graph problems. As a result of the linear algebraic manipulation, we could devise a linear-time algorithm for the problem in P.
results.title: A Note on Edge-based Graph Partitioning and its Linear Algebraic Structure

(1) poor connectivity. due to the limitation of the construction algorithm, the connectivity of the graph index is poor, which in turn affects the search performance. raw_metadata.content: partitioning large power-law graphs under memory constraints ruben mayer technical university of munich ruben.mayer@tum.de abstract distributed systems that manage and process graph-structured data internally solve a graph partitioning problem to minimize their com- munication overhead and query run-time. besides computational complexity—optimal graph partitioning is np-hard—another im- portant consideration is the memory overhead. real-world graphs often have an immense size, such that loading the complete graph into memory for partitioning is not economical or feasible. cur- rently, the common approach to reduce memory overhead is to rely on streaming partitioning algorithms. while the latest streaming algorithms lead to reasonable partitioning quality on some graphs, they are still not completely competitive to in-memory partitioners. in this paper, we propose a new system, hybrid edge partitioner (hep), that can partition graphs that fit partly into memory while yielding a high partitioning quality. hep can flexibly adapt its memory overhead by separating the edge set of the graph into two sub-sets. one sub-set is partitioned by ne++, a novel, efficient in-memory algorithm, while the other sub-set is partitioned by a streaming approach. our evaluations on large real-world graphs show that in many cases, hep outperforms both in-memory parti- tioning and streaming partitioning at the same time. hence, hep is an attractive alternative to existing solutions that cannot fine- tune their memory overheads. finally, we show that using hep, we achieve a significant speedup of distributed graph processing jobs on spark/graphx compared to state-of-the-art partitioning algorithms. ccs concepts • information systems → graph-based database models; • the- ory of computation → graph algorithms analysis. keywords graph partitioning; distributed graph processing acm reference format: ruben mayer and hans-arno jacobsen. 2021. hybrid edge partitioner: parti-

raw_metadata.content: A Note on Edge-based Graph Partitioning and its Linear Algebraic StructureLinear algebraEdge-centric representationGraph partitioningComputational complexityWe analyze two essential problems arising from edge-based graph partitioning. We show that one of them is an NP-hard problem but the other is in P, presenting a novel methodology that links linear algebra theory to the graph problems as a part of proving the facts. This is a significant trial in that linear algebra, which has been mostly adopted as a theoretical analysis tool, is practically applied to solving actual graph problems. As a result of the linear algebraic manipulation, we could devise a linear-time algorithm for the problem in P.

(1) poor connectivity. due to the limitation of the construction algorithm, the connectivity of the graph index is poor, which in turn affects the search performance. (2) redundant search. existing search algorithms use sufficiently long search steps for all queries to achieve high search accuracy. however, the query search steps follow the long-tailed distribution that brings the redundant search, e.g., for more than 40% of the queries, 87% of the search overhead is redundant. we propose two optimization strategies to tackle the above challenges. (1) reverse connection enhancement strategy. in the graph construction process, we increase the in-degree of the point to be inserted to enhance the graph connectivity, while keeping the out-degree low to maintain the high search efficiency. raw_metadata.content: 叶可江 研究员、博士生导师 中国科学院深圳先进技术研究院 云计算技术研究中心主任 电子邮件: kj.ye@siat.ac.cn 邮政编码: 518055 个人简介 叶可江,博士,研究员,博士生导师,中国科学院深圳先进技术研究院云计算研究中心主任。浙江大学计算机专业博士,澳大利亚悉尼大学联培博士(国家公派),美国卡内基梅隆大学博士后,国家重点研发计划项目负责人、国家自然科学基金委重大研究计划培育项目负责人、广东省粤港澳研究团队项目负责人。 主要研究方向为 人工智能系统及应用 ,在包括EuroSys、ISCA、ASPLOS、SC、SIGCOMM、INFOCOM等高水平会议和TOCS、TC、TPDS、ToN、TMC、TSC等高水平期刊发表论文200余篇,获最佳论文奖7次,出版专著1部《DartCloud:云基础设施服务平台》(科学出版社),授权中、美、澳、加发明专利100余件,牵头/参与制定标准5项,获软件著作版权20余件。主持国家重点研发计划项目(2项)、国家自然科学基金项目(3项)、及中科院、广东省、深圳市等重点类项目20余项。连续获得7期阿里巴巴创新研究计划资助,获得2021年CCF-华为胡杨林基金探索A类项目(操作系统领域)资助。 中国计算机学会杰出会员、杰出演讲者、第12届/13届全国会员代表,体系结构/系统软件/服务计算专委会委员,担任教育部、工信部、科技部、国家自然科学基金委、广东省及深圳市科技项目评审专家,担任Nature Electronics等20个期刊的审稿人,担任多个国际会议的程序会员会主席/共同主席/委员,担任CCF B类期刊JCST的青年编委。 曾获得中国电子学会科技进步一等奖、中国计算机学会服务计算青年才俊奖、中国科学院广州分院“优秀青年科技工作者”、2022年阿里巴巴“优秀学术合作奖”及云计算顶会ACM SoCC 2021最佳论文奖(国内首次)。 海外优青招聘启事 : 团队常年招聘国家自然科学基金“海外优青”项目候选人,热烈欢迎国外计算机相关专业优秀人才加入。 高层次人才招聘启事 : 团队常年招聘研究员、副研究员、助理研究员及博士后等各类高层次人才,热烈欢迎国内外计算机相关专业背景人员加入。 081203-计算机应用技术 085400-电子信息 云计算与大数据 近期论文 Y. Lin, V. Liu, T. Luo, C. Xu, K. Ye . Connex: Endpoint Mobility Primitives for Dynamic LLM Serving, ACM Special Interest Group on Data Communication (SIGCOMM) , 2026. (CCF A)
